A Holter monitor was revealing for frequent monomorphic PVCs up to 852 per hour (24.1%). As part of further work up, an echo was done which showed mildly dilated LV with EF 40-45% with global hypokinesis, normal RV and mildly dilated LA. The pt underwent cardiac MRI at ___ which showed global hypokinesis, a mildly dilated left ventricle with EF 37% and no evidence of gadolinium enhancement or abnormal perfusion.Since then, the pt has been trialed on metoprolol titrated up to 50mg, however repeat Holter monitoring did not show improvement in PVCs. She also was started briefly on flecanide, but it was not tolerated due to headaches. She presented to ___ on ___ for elective PVC ablation and electrophysiology studies. During the procedure, the pt's baseline rhythm was observed to be sinus at with ventricular bigeminy. There were frequent, monomorphic PVCs with a LBB and inferior axis with transition. While conducting mapping studies, a pericardial effusion was noted on ICE so the procedure was aborted. Shortly after, the pt suffered a PEA arrest and CPR was initiated, no medications were used, with successful achievement of ROSC. A pericardiocentesis was performed by interventional cardiology and a pericardial drain was placed w/ immediate sanguineous output of 170cc. The pt was mentating, maintaining adequate BPs, sat'ing well on a non rebreather and transferred to the CCU for further management. Total fluid received during the procedure was estimated to be about 2000cc of crystalloids. On arrival to the CCU the pt was experiencing significant chest pain from chest compressions and complained that it was causing her to have trouble breathing.
